_comment: Tunable knobs for daemon.py. Edit this file and restart the daemon (launchctl kickstart -k, or just quit/relaunch the process) to pick up changes -- no code edit needed. All intervals are in seconds.
_telegram_poll_interval_seconds_comment: Pause between listen.sh calls. Now 1s because listen.sh long-polls (telegram_long_poll_seconds, default 20): Telegram holds the call open and returns the moment a message lands.
_clickup_check_interval_seconds_comment: How often a `claude -p` call is made to check the ClickUp list set in profile.json (clickup_list_id) for anything due/upcoming/newly commented. Default 10 min.
_calendar_check_interval_seconds_comment: How often a `claude -p` call is made to check today's Google Calendar for anything upcoming/changed. Default 10 min.
_queue_drain_interval_seconds_comment: How often the daemon checks pending.json. If empty, this costs ZERO claude calls -- the check is a local file read. Default 15 min per spec.
_lock_stale_seconds_comment: If .daemon.lock is older than this, it is assumed to belong to a dead/crashed process and is reclaimed. Should be comfortably longer than claude_timeout_seconds.
_claude_timeout_seconds_comment: Hard timeout for any single `claude -p` subprocess call, so a hung call can't wedge a loop forever.
_log_max_bytes_comment: daemon.log rotates to daemon.log.1 past this size (5 MiB default).
_mail_whatsapp_comment: Both TODO -- neither is connected yet. Flags exist so a future loop can be added here without a schema change; daemon.py currently does not start loops for either.
